content:
The independent committee hearing for Wang Fuk Court has revealed that the management company "置邦興業" once compiled a file titled "Units Authorising Wong Bik-Kiu," showing that at the owners' meeting on 11 December 2021 to appoint consultant "鴻毅," 131 proxy votes were linked to Wong Bik-Kiu's team, accounting for about 25% of all proxy votes that day. After obtaining the authorisation records, 《集誌社》discovered that the 131 proxy votes authorised 53 people including Wong Bik-Kiu. Using these 53 names as a basis, Wong Bik-Kiu's "friendly" proxy votes that day reached 252, nearly half of the total. What is the background of this vast network? Five of these individuals share the same names as former Tai Wo Estate owners' corporation committee members; that owners' corporation was ousted in 2016 amid a dispute over an exorbitant renovation contract. Some former Tai Wo Estate committee members also "crossed estates" to appear at the Wang Fuk Court owners' meeting in December 2021. A review of records shows that the consultant "浩熙" involved in the Tai Wo Estate renovation dispute won the contract at a low price, and its company had bid for Wang Fuk Court projects. When "浩熙" served as consultant for King Tin Court in Tai Wai, "宏業" won the construction contract, and owners had filed a lawsuit alleging bid-rigging. The reporter contacted Wong Bik-Kiu via text message, email, and through a district councillor's office, but received no reply before deadline. Related reports: Investigation into Wong Bik-Kiu's Proxy Votes · Part 2 | 53 People Obtained 131 Proxy Votes — Who Are They? Some Have DAB, New Territories Association of Societies, and Other Affiliations; Investigation into Wong Bik-Kiu's Proxy Votes · Part 3 | After Two Owners Passed Away, Their Names Appeared on the "Units Authorising Wong Bik-Kiu" List — Families Were Unaware

The hearing revealed that Wang Fuk Court held an owners' meeting on 11 December 2021, with 131 proxy votes linked to Wong Bik-Kiu's team. The agenda that day included appointing project consultant "鴻毅" and demanding the replacement of the incumbent owners' corporation. (Owners' corporation photo)

The hearing revealed that Wong Bik-Kiu initially admitted to holding only about 20 proxy votes, but the committee found a file named "Units Authorising Wong Bik-Kiu" from management company "合安," documenting that she had 131 proxy votes at the 2021 meeting, representing about 25% of proxy votes that day. Most of the 131 proxy votes were not made out to Wong Bik-Kiu as the proxy holder. Wong later explained through her lawyer that this number was a combined total involving volunteer teams, incumbent owners' corporation committee members, community friends, etc., who together "helped process" 131 votes, with only slightly more than 20 specifically authorising her personally.

《集誌社》obtained multiple owners' meeting proxy vote records from Wang Fuk Court, including those from the meeting on 25 January 2019 to appoint "鴻毅" as the Registered Inspector (RI), the meeting on 11 December 2021 to appoint "鴻毅" as consultant, the meeting on 28 January 2024 to appoint "宏業" as contractor, the meeting on 6 September 2024 to appoint the new owners' corporation, as well as the "Units Authorising Wong Bik-Kiu" file.

In December 2021, former Tai Wo Estate owners' corporation chairwoman Tam Lai-ha (left), treasurer Shek Yuk-jing (front centre), committee member Wu Ling-lan (back centre), and Mok Shuk-ching (right) appeared at the Wang Fuk Court owners' meeting. On that day, Mok Shuk-ching was seen holding a stack of papers standing near the "proxy vote registration area." (Photo provided by interviewee)

Former Owners' Corporation of Tai Wo Estate, Involved in Renovation Dispute, Appears at Wang Fuk Court Meeting

The 131 proxy votes at the December 2021 owners' meeting involved 129 owners, with the first proxy holders being 53 people including Wong Bik-Kiu. Among them, "Tam Lai-ha," "Shek Yuk-jing," "Mok Shuk-ching," "Yiu Kam-sheung," and "Wu Ling-lan" each held 3 to 4 proxy votes, totalling 17. These five people share the same names as former Tai Wo Estate owners' corporation committee members — Tam Lai-ha was former chairwoman, Shek Yuk-jing was former treasurer, and the other three were former committee members.

Source A (alias), a former Tai Wo Estate Mutual Aid Committee member concerned about renovation and owners' corporation disputes, visited the Wang Fuk Court owners' meeting venue in December 2021. She recalled that upon arrival, she noticed several former Tai Wo Estate owners' corporation committee members, including Tam Lai-ha, Shek Yuk-jing, Mok Shuk-ching, and Wu Ling-lan, present. "At the time I found it very strange, they were acting like hosts, with Wong Bik-Kiu greeting everyone at the venue… One or two people showing up would not be unusual, but an entire team, boss… My gut feeling was that they were involved again." Source A provided photos from the day, pointing out that Mok Shuk-ching was holding a stack of papers by the "proxy vote registration area," constantly making phone calls "wandering around" and "queuing up to collect voting forms."

In 2016, Tai Wo Estate was embroiled in a bid-rigging dispute over an exorbitant renovation contract. The then owners' corporation eventually re-tendered, and the project cost was reduced from HK$27 million to HK$500,000–700,000. The owners' corporation was subsequently ousted.

Regarding the Tai Wo Estate bid-rigging dispute, Source A said that Tai Wo residents had inquired with the Housing Department's ICU, which supervised the project, and learned that the government repair order only involved a small portion of the exterior walls of buildings where concrete spalling had occurred. However, the owners' corporation decided without consulting residents to renovate the entire exterior walls of all three buildings, and used the argument that the estate maintenance fund had over HK$100 million and residents would not need to contribute, to lobby residents. When residents sought to understand the decision, the owners' corporation refused owners' attendance at meetings, citing a limit of five participants.

According to records, the rental-purchase public housing estate Tai Wo Estate was embroiled in an exorbitant renovation dispute in 2016. Tam Lai-ha and Shek Yuk-jing were the then owners' corporation chairwoman and treasurer, while Yiu Kam-sheung, Mok Shuk-ching, and Wu Ling-lan were committee members. The owners' corporation hired consultant "浩熙建築工程顧問公司" to conduct an exterior wall survey, with a consultancy fee of about HK$150,000. The renovation quotation for the exterior walls of the three buildings reached as high as HK$27 million, with each household bearing over HK$10,000. The project costs sparked a bid-rigging dispute, and after residents' efforts, re-tendering took place, reducing the project cost to HK$500,000–700,000. The old owners' corporation was ousted that same year.

Tam Lai-ha (seventh from left) ran for the District Council under the DAB banner in 2003 and lost. She served as chairwoman of the Tai Wo Estate owners' corporation from the early 2000s until being ousted in 2016. The photo shows a group photo at the 2015 Tai Po Rural Committee inauguration dinner, with Wong Bik-Kiu at second from left. (Facebook photo)

Former Tai Wo Estate Owners' Corporation Chairwoman Is DAB Associate

Former Tai Wo Estate owners' corporation chairwoman Tam Lai-ha, who held proxy votes and appeared on Wang Bik-Kiu's authorisation list, has a DAB background. She ran under the party in the 2003 Tai Po District Council election and lost, while her party affiliate Wong Bik-Kiu won. In 2006, Tam Lai-ha was appointed as an additional member of the Tai Po District Council Culture, Recreation and Sports Committee. During the New Territories East by-election in September 2016, she canvassed for DAB candidates Chan Hak-kan and Chow Ho-ting. Former committee member Mok Shuk-ching served alongside Wong Bik-Kiu on the Tai Po District Fight Crime Committee in 2009, and was a specially invited director of the New Territories Association of Societies in 2021; Yiu Kam-sheung is also a Tai Po district director of the New Territories Association of Societies; Shek Yuk-jing and Wu Ling-lan are current members of the Tai Po Po Nga district Care Team.

Apart from the December 2021 owners' meeting to appoint "鴻毅," "Shek Yuk-jing" and "Wu Ling-lan" each received one proxy vote at the September 2024 owners' meeting to appoint the new owners' corporation, with "Wong Chun-yau" listed as another proxy holder. According to records, "Wong Chun-yau" and Wong Bik-Kiu co-founded the "樂群義工聯盟" (Lok Kwan Volunteer Alliance).

The reporter contacted Wong Bik-Kiu via text message, email, and through a district councillor's office, but received no reply before deadline.

Wong Bik-Kiu co-founded "樂群義工聯盟" with Wong Chun-yau (left in photo) and Ting Kit-mui (right in photo). On the "Units Authorising Wong Bik-Kiu" list, there are proxy holders with the same names, as well as individuals with names related to "樂群義工" who received proxy votes. (Facebook photo)

Tai Wo Estate Consultant Previously Bid for Wang Fuk Court; 宏業 Won Contract for King Tin Court Project

"浩熙," which received ultra-low consultancy fees at Tai Wo Estate, was founded by Wong Siu-cheung, who also bid for Wang Fuk Court projects. In January 2019, "浩熙" bid HK$700,000 for the Wang Fuk Court Registered Inspector (RI) position, higher than "鴻毅"'s HK$220,000, and did not win.

By 2021, "大地建築顧問有限公司," where Wong Siu-cheung had served as director, bid HK$400,000 for the Wang Fuk Court consultant position, slightly higher than "鴻毅"'s HK$300,000, and did not win; "快利達建築工程顧問有限公司" bid HK$280,000 for the Wang Fuk Court consultant position and likewise did not win. Wong Siu-cheung became a director of "快利達" the following year.

According to court documents, in 2009, King Tin Court in Tai Wai hired "浩熙" as project consultant. After tendering in 2011, "宏業" was appointed as contractor for a project valued at HK$91 million. In 2012, an owner filed a lawsuit alleging bid-rigging in the project, seeking to have it overturned, but lost.

The company that won the Tai Wo Estate renovation consultancy contract at a low price in 2016 subsequently bid for the Wang Fuk Court Registered Inspector position, while an affiliated company bid for the Wang Fuk Court consultant position. Both bids were higher than 鴻毅's and neither succeeded.

Wong Siu-cheung and Wong Siu-keung, who was involved in the Sha Tin Chui Wu Garden bid-rigging case, are suspected to be related parties. During the trial of the HK$260 million Sha Tin Chui Wu bid-rigging case, it was revealed that Wong Siu-keung, a director of "環球屋宇," paid "tea money" and referral fees to owners' corporation members and project subcontractors, and arranged for shell companies to bid, enabling "環球屋宇" to win. In 2023, Wong Siu-keung was arrested in connection with an HK$160 million project bid-rigging case in Discovery Bay. Company registry records show that a construction company where Wong Siu-cheung previously served as director, now dissolved, used the same registered address as Wong Siu-keung.
